mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 320/350 CDI OM642 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 diesel is fundamentally robust and capable of 200,000+ miles, but it has a well-documented Achilles heel: oil cooler seal failure that allows coolant to mix with oil [1†L21-L23][10†L11-L12]. Catch it early and it's a great engine. Oil cooler seals fail at 70,000-120,000 miles - the £5 part that costs £650-£950 to replace [5†L6-L8]. Timing chain stretch can occur from 75,000 miles [3†L25-L27]. Swirl flap motor and turbo actuator failures are common on higher-mileage units [11†L22-L24][13†L28-L29]. Preventative seal replacement is strongly recommended [1†L26-L27].

mainEntity.name: What is the oil cooler seal problem on the Mercedes CLS 320/350 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 engine has rubber oil cooler seals at the centre of the Vee that degrade and leak. When they fail, they cause oil to mix with coolant - a £5 part that requires 9 hours of labour to replace [5†L7-L8]. Oil cooler sits "in the bowels of hell deep down in the 'V' of the engine" [1†L18-L19]. Symptoms: oil traces in the inner-V, oil leaks at drain points [1†L12-L14]. Original orange seals replaced with updated purple seals [11†L21-L22]. Specialist seal replacement costs £650-£950 [5†L6-L8]. If ignored, coolant contamination can destroy the engine [1†L26-L27].

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLS 320/350 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained OM642 engines regularly exceed 200,000-300,000 miles [9†L4]. The OM642 is a robust engine that, with proper maintenance, can deliver exceptional longevity [7†L44-L46]. OM642: 200k-300k+ miles with regular servicing [9†L4]. Oil cooler seals need replacing once - typically at 70k-120k miles [5†L26]. historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLS 320/350 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLS 320 CDI and CLS 350 CDI are powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 turbodiesel - the engine that defined diesel motoring for the CLS across two generations. First introduced in the C219 CLS in 2005, the OM642 delivered 224 hp and 510 Nm of torque, combining effortless V6 refinement with genuine 40+ mpg economy. The CLS 350 CDI badge appeared from 2009, with later BlueTEC variants producing up to 265 hp and 620 Nm, making the CLS a true grand tourer.

milestones.description: CLS 320 CDI launched with OM642.920 3.0L V6 diesel, 224 hp, 510 Nm, 7G-TRONIC transmission
CLS 350 CDI badge introduced (same OM642.920 engine, 224 hp) from April 2009
C218 second-generation CLS launched with OM642 LS (BlueTEC) engines
2014 - CLS 350 CDI (OM642.853/OM642.854) with 265 hp, 620 Nm, twin-turbo configuration
2017 - CLS 350 BlueTEC with OM642 LS Eco2 and 9G-TRONIC transmission
CLS diesel production ends; OM642 continues in other Mercedes models

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLS 320/350 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLS 320 CDI and CLS 350 CDI are powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel - an engine that defined Mercedes diesel excellence for over a decade. However, the OM642 has a well-documented Achilles heel: oil cooler seal failure. This £5 part requires 9 hours of labour to replace, and if ignored, can lead to catastrophic engine failure. Timing chain stretch, swirl flap motor failure, and turbo actuator problems are also common on higher-mileage examples. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Cooler Seal Failure - The OM642's Defining Weakness
problems.rootCause: The rubber oil cooler seals at the centre of the Vee degrade and crack under repeated heat cycles, allowing engine oil and coolant to mix. The original orange seals were replaced with updated purple seals in later production. Symptoms include oil traces in the inner-V of the engine, oil leaks at the drain points, and in severe cases, coolant contamination and low oil pressure warnings.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil cooler seals with upgraded Viton seals, flush cooling system, change oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: 70k-120k miles; excellent value if caught before contamination

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil cooler seals plus turbocharger if oil starvation has damaged bearings
repairOptions.longevity: Restores full performance; viable if bottom end is still healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt OM642 with upgraded seals, new oil cooler, timing components, and bench testing
repairOptions.longevity: Required if coolant contamination has damaged bearings

problems.recommendation: The oil cooler seal failure is the single most significant problem affecting the OM642 engine. If you own a CLS 320 CDI or CLS 350 CDI with over 70,000 miles, preventative seal replacement is strongly recommended - it's the best insurance policy you can buy for your engine. Don't wait for symptoms - oil traces in the inner-V or on the under tray are warning signs. If you already have coolant contamination or oil pressure warnings, a rebuilt engine with upgraded seals is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes CLS 320/350 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - The OM642's Second Weakness
problems.rootCause: The OM642 uses a duplex roller chain camshaft drive. Early engines had "lifetime" duplex chains, but around 2009-2010 there were many chain redesigns resulting in accelerated wear, with some requiring replacement in as little as 75,000 miles. A stretched chain can damage the balance shaft and cam sprockets if allowed to continue. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start for 1-2 seconds, and if the tensioner piston extends beyond 10mm, replacement is required.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; tensioner wear only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
Supply & fit fully rebuilt OM642 with new timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped and valves have contacted pistons

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start for 1-2 seconds is the early warning sign of timing chain wear. Don't ignore it - specialist timing chain replacement at £1,400-£2,000 resolves the issue if done promptly. If the chain has already slipped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the only safe option.

problems.group: Swirl Flap Motor & Intake Manifold Failure
problems.h4: Swirl Flap Motor & Intake Manifold Failure - Loss of Power and Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The swirl flap motor fails, causing the engine to enter limp mode. Oil leaks from the turbo oil seal can contaminate the swirl flap motor, leading to a £500+ repair. The engine can work fine without the swirl flaps in operation, and a resistor can be fitted to bypass the failed motor. However, if flaps break, fragments can enter cylinders and cause catastrophic damage.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if motor failure only; flaps still intact

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace complete intake manifold with swirl flap assembly
repairOptions.longevity: Required if flaps are broken or damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 with new intake manifold, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if swirl flap fragments have damaged cylinders

problems.recommendation: Loss of power and limp mode are classic signs of swirl flap motor failure. A £250-£400 motor replacement resolves the issue if caught early. If the flaps themselves are damaged, a replacement intake manifold at £550-£850 is required. Catch it early - flap debris in the cylinders can cause catastrophic engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM642 swirl flap repair for your Mercedes CLS 350 CDI

problems.h4: Turbocharger Actuator Failure - Boost Loss and Poor Performance
problems.rootCause: The electronic turbocharger actuator fails due to worn motor brushes or broken solder connections. Symptoms include poor acceleration, very little power at highway speed, and juddering when hot. The actuator sits on the turbo and requires removal of the Y-pipe and heat shield to access.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; actuator failure only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace turbocharger with reconditioned unit, new actuator
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbocharger itself is damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 with new turbo and actuator, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo debris has circulated through the engine

problems.recommendation: Loss of power and poor acceleration are classic signs of turbo actuator failure. A specialist can often diagnose this with a diagnostic scan. Actuator replacement at £350-£550 resolves the issue if caught early. If the turbo itself has failed, full turbo replacement is required.
